content.title: About
content.content: The vanilla sandwich cookie consists of two soft cookies with a creamy vanilla filling between them. The cookies are lightly sweet, while the filling offers a delicate vanilla aroma. It is popular as a light snack and dessert.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first vanilla sandwich cookie recipe appeared in the United States in the early 1920s.
Traditional filling is made from butter, sugar and natural vanilla extract.
The cookies are often served at children’s parties and school lunchboxes.
Vanilla aroma intensifies when the cookies are stored in an airtight package at room temperature.
Many filling variations exist, including chocolate, nuts or fruit purées.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide a quick boost of energy, convenient for active individuals.

items.title: Contains a modest amount of calcium
items.content: Calcium from the dairy components of the filling supports bone health.

items.title: Vanilla extract
items.content: Vanilla has antioxidant properties and may help improve mood.

items.title: Small amount of protein
items.content: Protein from dairy helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Moderate fat content
items.content: Fats from butter supply fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The filling contains milk and butter, which can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The product is calorie‑dense due to sugar; consumption should be moderate.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: The cookie dough contains wheat, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Risk of overconsumption
items.content: The light texture may encourage eating large quantities quickly.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie is convenient to eat straight from the pack, as a sweet accompaniment to coffee or tea, or placed in a child’s lunchbox. The filling can be gently warmed in a microwave to become softer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in an airtight package. For longer shelf life, keep refrigerated to prevent the filling from softening. Discard if the product develops an off smell or taste.
